# africa-payments-webhooks

> Open-source library (MIT) to verify and normalise payment webhooks from African payment providers — Paystack,
> Flutterwave (v3 verif-hash and v4 flutterwave-signature), Monnify, Squad, Korapay, Fincra, Interswitch and Nomba — in
> JavaScript/TypeScript (npm: `africa-payments-webhooks`; Node.js 20+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js, AWS Lambda,
> Express, Fastify, NestJS, Koa, Hono) and Python (PyPI: `africa-payments-webhooks`; Django, Flask, FastAPI). Zero dependencies.

Use it when a developer needs to: verify a Paystack webhook signature (x-paystack-signature, HMAC-SHA512), verify a
Flutterwave webhook (verif-hash / flutterwave-signature), verify a Monnify webhook (monnify-signature), verify Squad
(x-squad-encrypted-body), Korapay (x-korapay-signature), Fincra (signature), Interswitch (X-Interswitch-Signature) or
Nomba (nomba-signature) webhooks; handle duplicate/retried payment webhooks; or support several Nigerian/African payment
providers behind one webhook endpoint with one event shape (payment.succeeded, transfer.failed, refund.processed…).

Key facts: verification uses the raw request body and constant-time comparison; every adapter returns 400
`body_already_parsed` if the framework already parsed the JSON; amounts are reported with explicit units (Paystack/Squad
in kobo = minor, Flutterwave/Monnify/Korapay/Fincra/Nomba in naira = major); Monnify does not sign sandbox webhooks
(`allowUnsignedSandbox`); Flutterwave v3 and Nomba require re-verifying the transaction via the provider API.


<!-- guide/getting-started -->
# Getting started

```sh
npm install africa-payments-webhooks     # Node, Bun, Deno, Workers, Next.js
pip install africa-payments-webhooks     # Django, Flask, FastAPI
```

## One-step handler (recommended)

```ts
import { fetchWebhook } from 'africa-payments-webhooks/web';   // Next.js App Router, Hono, Workers, Deno, Bun

export const POST = fetchWebhook({
  provider: 'paystack',
  secret: process.env.PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY!,
  onEvent: async (event) => {
    if (event.type === 'payment.succeeded') await markOrderPaid(event.reference);
  },
});
```

The handler verifies the signature, parses the event, skips duplicates (when you pass a `store`), calls `onEvent`,
and answers the provider correctly: **200** (empty body), **401** for bad signatures, **400** for a parsed body,
**500** if your `onEvent` throws (so the provider retries).

| Import | Framework |
|---|---|
| `africa-payments-webhooks/web` | Next.js App Router, Hono (`c.req.raw`), Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Remix, SvelteKit |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/express` | Express 4/5 |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/fastify` | Fastify 4/5 |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/nestjs` | NestJS |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/koa` | Koa |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/next` | Next.js Pages Router |
| `africa-payments-webhooks/lambda` | AWS Lambda |

## Low-level API

```ts
import { verify, parse, detectProvider } from 'africa-payments-webhooks';

const result = await verify('monnify', { rawBody, headers, secret });
// { ok: true, provider } | { ok: false, provider, code, message }
const event = parse('monnify', rawBody);
```

Error codes: `missing_signature`, `invalid_signature`, `malformed_signature`, `timestamp_out_of_range`,
`ip_not_allowed`, `body_already_parsed`, `invalid_body`, `unknown_provider`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `secret` | — | String, array (rotation) or per-provider object |
| `store` | none | Duplicate protection (see [Duplicate events](./idempotency)) |
| `ttlSeconds` | 259200 | How long to remember event ids (72 h) |
| `ipAllowlist` | `false` | `true` = provider-published IPs; or your own list/CIDRs. An extra check, never sufficient alone |
| `allowUnsignedSandbox` | `false` | Monnify sandbox sends no signature. **Never enable in production** |
| `toleranceSeconds` | 300 | Nomba replay window (`0` disables) |
| `onError` | — | Called with `{ code, message }` on failures (never contains secrets) |


<!-- guide/raw-body -->
# The raw-body rule

Providers sign the **exact bytes** they send. If your framework parses the JSON first, the bytes are gone and
verification fails — this is the #1 webhook bug. Every adapter detects a pre-parsed body and returns
**400 `body_already_parsed`** instead of failing silently.

| Framework | What to do |
|---|---|
| **Express** | Route-level `express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })`. If you need a global `express.json()`, add `verify: (req, _res, buf) => { req.rawBody = buf }` — the adapter reads `req.rawBody` first. |
| **Fastify** | Register the route inside a scoped plugin and call `useRawJsonBody(scope)`. |
| **NestJS** | `NestFactory.create(AppModule, { rawBody: true })`. Don't set `bodyParser: false`. |
| **Koa** | Use `@koa/bodyparser` — it exposes `ctx.request.rawBody`. |
| **Next.js App Router, Hono, Workers, Deno, Bun** | Nothing. `fetchWebhook` reads `request.arrayBuffer()`. With Hono, pass `c.req.raw`. |
| **Next.js Pages Router** | `export const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } }` in the route file. |
| **AWS Lambda** | Nothing. Base64 bodies (`isBase64Encoded`) are decoded for you. |
| **Django** | Nothing — `request.body` is raw. |
| **Flask** | Nothing — the helper uses `request.get_data()`. Don't read `request.json` first. |
| **FastAPI** | Don't declare a Pydantic body parameter on the webhook route. |

**Proxies and gateways** that re-encode JSON (some API gateways, some no-code tools) also break signatures — forward
bodies untouched.


<!-- guide/providers -->
# Providers

| Provider | Header | Algorithm & key | Signed input | Amount unit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paystack | `x-paystack-signature` | HMAC-SHA512 hex · secret key | raw body | minor (kobo) | documented |
| Flutterwave v3 | `verif-hash` | equals your dashboard *secret hash* | — (no body integrity) | major | documented |
| Flutterwave v4 | `flutterwave-signature` | HMAC-SHA256 base64 · secret hash | raw body | major | beta |
| Monnify | `monnify-signature` | HMAC-SHA512 hex · client secret | raw body | major | **verified** |
| Squad (gateway) | `x-squad-encrypted-body` | HMAC-SHA512 hex (upper) · secret key | raw body | minor (kobo) | documented |
| Korapay | `x-korapay-signature` | HMAC-SHA256 hex · secret key | the `data` object only | major | documented |
| Fincra | `signature` | HMAC-SHA512 hex · **webhook** secret | payload | major | documented |
| Interswitch | `X-Interswitch-Signature` | HMAC-SHA512 hex · webhook secret | raw body | minor | documented |
| Nomba | `nomba-signature` + `nomba-timestamp` | HMAC-SHA256 base64 · signature key | selected fields + timestamp | major | **verified** |

**Status:** *verified* = the provider's published test vector reproduces in our CI; *documented* = implemented
exactly as the official docs describe (no vector published); *beta* = the provider's docs are inconsistent.

## Provider notes

- **Paystack** — sends only from `52.31.139.75`, `52.49.173.169`, `52.214.14.220`. Retries every 3 min ×4, then hourly
  for 72 h. There is no `charge.failed` webhook. Re-verify with `GET /transaction/verify/:reference`.
- **Flutterwave** — v3's `verif-hash` is a shared secret, not a body signature: **always** re-verify with
  `GET /v3/transactions/{id}/verify`. v4 accounts send `flutterwave-signature`; we pick the scheme by header.
  Retries (if enabled): 3 times, 30 min apart.
- **Monnify** — its docs' prose says "SHA-512(secret + body)", but its own published example only reproduces as
  HMAC-SHA512 (we test both facts). **Sandbox notifications are unsigned** — use `allowUnsignedSandbox` only in sandbox.
  Single source IP `35.242.133.146`.
- **Squad** — gateway notifications only (`x-squad-encrypted-body`, source IP `18.133.63.109`). Virtual-account
  notifications use a different scheme and are planned.
- **Korapay** — signs only `JSON.stringify(body.data)`. We verify the exact `data` bytes received first, then the
  compact re-serialisation.
- **Fincra** — key is the **webhook encryption key**, not your API secret; sandbox and live keys differ.
- **Interswitch** — reply **200 with no body** (the handler does). `TRANSACTION.COMPLETED` is not success — check
  `responseCode === "00"` (the parser does).
- **Nomba** — the only provider that signs a timestamp (replay window enforced). **Amounts are not signed** —
  re-verify via Nomba's API. Its docs print the example signature with a lowercase first letter and its samples compare
  case-insensitively, so we do too (in constant time).

## Planned
Squad virtual accounts, OPay (HMAC-SHA3-512 over a field template), Paga (SHA-512 field hashes), and **unsigned
callback helpers** for M-Pesa Daraja and MTN MoMo (URL token, optional IP allowlist, mandatory status query).


<!-- guide/idempotency -->
# Duplicate events

Providers retry deliveries (Paystack for 72 hours), and networks duplicate requests. Pass a `store`:

```ts
interface IdempotencyStore {
  claim(id: string, ttlSeconds: number): boolean | Promise<boolean>; // true = first time we see it
  release?(id: string): void | Promise<void>;                        // called if onEvent throws
}
```

**Redis**
```ts
const store = {
  claim: async (id, ttl) => (await redis.set(`wh:${id}`, '1', 'EX', ttl, 'NX')) === 'OK',
  release: async (id) => void (await redis.del(`wh:${id}`)),
};
```

**Postgres**
```sql
CREATE TABLE webhook_events (id text PRIMARY KEY, seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());
```
```ts
const store = {
  claim: async (id) => (await sql`INSERT INTO webhook_events (id) VALUES (${id}) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`).length > 0,
  release: async (id) => void (await sql`DELETE FROM webhook_events WHERE id = ${id}`),
};
```

`event.id` is `provider:providerEventType:providerReference[:status]`, so a *status change* (e.g. Flutterwave
`pending → successful`) is processed, but a retry of the same status is not. `MemoryIdempotencyStore` is for
development only. **Also make your fulfilment idempotent** (e.g. "mark order paid if not already paid").


<!-- guide/testing -->
# Testing your handler

`signTestPayload` produces a body + headers exactly as the provider would sign them:

```ts
import { signTestPayload } from 'africa-payments-webhooks/testing';

const { body, headers } = await signTestPayload(
  'paystack',
  { event: 'charge.success', data: { id: 1, reference: 'order-42', amount: 500000, currency: 'NGN', status: 'success' } },
  process.env.PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY_TEST!,
);
const res = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/webhooks/paystack', { method: 'POST', body, headers });
```

Nomba: pass `{ timestamp: '2026-11-12T10:00:00Z' }`. Flutterwave v3: pass `{ flutterwaveVersion: 'v3' }`.

Python:
```python
from africa_payments_webhooks.testing import sign_test_payload
body, headers = sign_test_payload("monnify", {"eventType": "SUCCESSFUL_TRANSACTION", "eventData": {...}}, SECRET)
```


<!-- guide/security -->
# Security model

- Signatures are checked over the **raw bytes**, with **constant-time** comparison. Malformed signatures are rejected
  without exceptions.
- The library never logs secrets, signatures or payloads, and its error messages never contain them.
- **Webhooks say "something happened"; the API says exactly what.** Re-confirm the transaction (amount, currency,
  status, reference) with the provider's API before giving value. This is **mandatory** for:
  - Flutterwave v3 (`verif-hash` doesn't protect the body),
  - Nomba (amounts aren't covered by the signature),
  - M-Pesa / MTN MoMo (unsigned callbacks — planned helpers).
- Only Nomba signs a timestamp. For the others, a captured webhook can be replayed — use a `store` and make
  fulfilment idempotent.
- `ipAllowlist` is defence in depth only; behind proxies make sure `sourceIp` is the real client IP.
- Rotate secrets with `secret: [newSecret, oldSecret]`, then remove the old one.
- Report vulnerabilities privately — see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/evergreenesoftware/africa-payments-webhooks/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

This library is provided "as is" (MIT). It does not move money; you remain responsible for your payment logic.


<!-- guide/python -->
# Python

```sh
pip install africa-payments-webhooks
```
Same providers, behaviour and test vectors as the npm package (a shared fixture file guarantees parity).

**Django**
```python
from africa_payments_webhooks.adapters.django import webhook_view
urlpatterns = [path("webhooks/paystack/", webhook_view(provider="paystack", secret=settings.PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY, on_event=on_event))]
```

**Flask**
```python
from africa_payments_webhooks.adapters.flask import webhook_view
app.add_url_rule("/webhooks/monnify", view_func=webhook_view(provider="monnify", secret=SECRET, on_event=on_event), methods=["POST"], endpoint="monnify")
```

**FastAPI** (`on_event` may be async)
```python
from africa_payments_webhooks.adapters.fastapi import webhook_endpoint
app.add_api_route("/webhooks/flutterwave", webhook_endpoint(provider="flutterwave", secret=SECRET, on_event=on_event), methods=["POST"])
```

**Low level**
```python
from africa_payments_webhooks import verify, parse, handle_webhook
result = verify("korapay", raw_body=raw_bytes, headers=headers, secret=SECRET)   # truthy when ok
event = parse("korapay", raw_bytes)                                              # PaymentEvent dataclass
```
